[Figure: This graph shows an exponential distribution. The graph slopes downward. It begins at a point on the y-axis and approaches the x-axis at the right edge of the graph. The region under the graph from x = 6 to x = 7 is shaded.]

  Figure 
5.41

6. 

For a continuous probablity distribution, 0 ≤ x ≤ 15. What is P(x > 15)?

7. 

What is the area under f(x) if the function is a continuous probability density function?

8. 

For a continuous probability distribution, 0 ≤ x ≤ 10. What is P(x = 7)?

9. 

A continuous probability function is restricted to the portion between x = 0 and 7. What is P(x = 10)?

10. 

f(x) for a continuous probability function is 15" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">15\(\frac{1}{5}\), and the function is restricted to 0 ≤ x ≤ 5. What is P(x < 0)?

Find the probability that x falls in the shaded area.

[Figure: This shows the graph of the function f(x) = 1 9, the pdf for a uniform distribution. A horizontal line ranges from the point (0, 1/9) to the point (9, 1/9). 5.42
